rationale: Full English article read (1,352 lines). The concrete board depicts an illegal snapshot shot hitting the sun and a legal straight-line fleet intercept at the rotating target's future position. A faint short arc denotes only planet motion. The adjacent deterministic Physics -> World model -> Strategy modules and committed-launches ledger capture the architecture and future-arrival update. Generated geometry was corrected twice: rejected line now actually hits the sun, and both target positions lie at the same orbital radius. No curved fleet flight, waypoint detour, learned-RL policy claim, or game result is shown.
alt_en: A straight fleet launch intercepts a moving planet at arrival, while a sun-crossing shot is rejected; physics, world model, strategy, and committed launches organize the agent.
alt_ko: 태양을 가로지르는 경로는 거부하고 움직이는 행성의 도착 시점 위치로 함대를 직선 발사하며, 물리·월드 모델·전략과 발사 기록으로 에이전트를 구성한다.
prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: clear, professional technical blog cover for the Orbit Wars game-AI structured baseline; wide landscape approximately 1.9:1.
Primary request: concretely show safe straight-line fleet interception of a moving planet, together with a small three-layer agent architecture. The main left two-thirds is a clean top-down square strategy board on white. One blue source planet appears at left; a muted ochre sun sits near the centre-lower part of the board. The same target planet is shown at two positions around the sun: a pale outlined ghost lower-right labelled "Now" and a solid teal circle upper-right labelled "At arrival". A faint dotted circular orbit arc links the two target positions, showing planet motion only. One crisp straight teal fleet arrow goes from the source boundary directly to the future target's boundary, passing clearly above and outside the sun. A short row of tiny triangular fleet markers sits along this single straight line. A separate faint muted-red straight candidate line from the same source toward the current target crosses the sun and is stopped with a small cross at the sun, showing the rejected shot.
Right one-third: three clean stacked modules labelled exactly "Physics", "World model", "Strategy", connected downward by short crisp arrows. A small lower "Committed launches" ledger icon feeds a narrow return arrow into "World model", showing that accepted launches update the future-arrival forecast.
Concept accuracy: the baseline is deterministic planning, not a learned RL policy. Fleets travel in straight lines after launch; only planets rotate. The physics layer validates a direct, sun-safe shot and ETA; world model predicts owner/garrison at arrival; strategy ranks valid mission families; committed launches become future arrivals. Do not draw curving fleet trajectories or waypoint detours.
Text (verbatim), only these eight short labels: "Now", "At arrival", "Sun", "Direct shot", "Physics", "World model", "Strategy", "Committed launches". The first four belong to the clear board elements and direct route; the last four belong to the architecture. No title, coordinates, game score, quantitative results, ship counts, or additional text.
Style/medium: polished flat technical editorial illustration, crisp schematic geometry, clear circles and triangle fleets, subtle board outline, restrained white/off-white #F7F8F7 backdrop, slate #334A5A outlines, muted blue #658CB2 and teal #488A8A. Tiny warm ochre sun and muted red rejection accent are acceptable. No painterly texture, glossy 3D, photorealism, glow, nebula, or dramatic sci-fi scenery.
Composition/framing: wide horizontal 1.9:1 image intended for 1200-by-630 blog display, generous margins, simple large legible English labels, safe central framing and a well-separated board and architecture. No dense tables or code. The valid launch and target's future position should be the dominant focal point. Deliver one finished cover image; no screenshot UI, logo, watermark, border, or fabricated performance statistics.

quality_review: Final generated source and encoded WebP inspected. Straight legal route, rejected route intersects sun, same-radius target positions with faint planet-motion arc, clear architecture labels and commitment feedback.
